You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Thus use the populated region to the right of the vertical line as a seed tile and propagate across its corresponding empty region; repeat the horizontal band pattern below the separator. ## task-6345fdba: diagonal-wave repetition around a cross separator

Solved test: 9x9 grid with full-height vertical line and full-width horizontal line of color 9, intersecting at (4,4) (0-indexed). Each of the four 4x4 quadrants carries the same 4x4 local pattern when expressed relative to its nearest cross boundaries, with the pattern oriented as a reflected/reversed diagonal wave. When test input appearance encourages an unverified transformation or demos suggest a global operation:
1. Treat task IDs, memory, and resemblance as priors only; confirm current evidence.
2. Without a grounded matching rule, request a demonstration instead of guessing. Seek examples that distinguish hypotheses.
3. Compare the complete input/output pair: dimensions, every changed cell, rows, columns, colors, and output regularities. Do not assume dominant test-object geometry controls the transformation.
4. State a rule that explains the whole demo and verify it against every cell before applying to the test.
5. Emit exactly one valid Continual-ARC JSON action, without prose.

Case note: task-a29c068e has context-dependent diagonal continuation. Prior test: bg8, 1 at (4,4),(5,3), 4 at (4,5),(5,6); correct extension was 1 down-left and 4 down-right to edge. Key lesson: extend only aligned repeated-color diagonal pair in the demonstrated direction; don't recolor unrelated endpoint colors. Each instance still requires confirmation of direction/context.

Balance demo cost against the risk of an unsupported submission. Treat rejection as evidence against the hypothesis, not as a cue for cosmetic variants.
